programme: HMGXB4's target set (ACTA2, MYH11, TAGLN, CNN1) is the canonical SRF/myocardin-driven smooth-muscle contractile gene program; HDAC7 sits on the repressive arm of the same circuit through its MEF2A/MEF2C/MEF2D targets (plus HIF1A and MMP10, tying it to hypoxia and matrix remodeling); TEAD1 supplies the Hippo-YAP/TAZ mechanotransduction input (via its SRF and VEGFA targets); MAML2, as obligate NOTCH1-HES1 coactivator, supplies the Notch arm that specifies smooth-muscle/arterial identity and cross-talks with the same MEF2/SRF node. Together these four form a mechanosensitive contractile-versus-synthetic state switch for smooth-muscle/mesenchymal-like cells, not a single-gene signal.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease this axis governs vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching in the vessel wall: HDAC7-MEF2 repression and Notch-MAML2 signaling normally hold VSMCs in the differentiated, contractile state defined by the HMGXB4 target genes (ACTA2/MYH11/TAGLN/CNN1); loss of that repression under altered wall stress, with TEAD1/Hippo-YAP reinforcing a proliferative, matrix-remodeling state, is the transcriptional substrate of medial remodeling and plaque formation.
role_in_b: In kidney papillary cell carcinoma the same module would be repurposed for tumor-stroma/vascular dedifferentiation rather than tubule epithelium per se: TEAD1/Hippo-YAP reactivation has documented growth-driving effects in renal carcinoma (via the SH3BGRL2-Hippo/TEAD axis, PMID 31911271, shown in clear cell RCC), and MAML2/Notch carries an Open Targets association specifically in kidney papillary carcinoma, consistent with a parallel dedifferentiation/proliferative signal in the tumor's mesenchymal/vascular compartment.
shared_axis: Both diseases pathologically flip the same smooth-muscle/mesenchymal contractile-to-proliferative switch in a supporting mesenchymal compartment — the vessel wall media in cardiovascular disease, tumor stroma and neovasculature in papillary renal carcinoma — using the same HDAC7-MEF2/Notch-MAML2/Hippo-TEAD wiring that normally holds HMGXB4's contractile target genes on.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target sets (a genuine, well-described smooth-muscle/mechanotransduction circuit), and TEAD1 and MAML2 each have a retrieved placement in kidney cancer (a PMID for TEAD1/Hippo in ccRCC, an Open Targets score for MAML2 in papillary RCC specifically). But nothing was retrieved for any factor in cardiovascular disease, so the CVD side of the account rests on general vascular biology rather than on anything in the record, and the kidney-side citation for TEAD1 is for clear cell, not papillary, RCC — hence moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 31911271 — shows Hippo/TEAD signaling (TEAD1's pathway) drives growth in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, supporting a role for this axis in kidney cancer generally, though not specifically papillary RCC or cardiovascular disease. No PMID retrieved for HMGXB4, HDAC7, or MAML2 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In matched atherosclerotic-plaque VSMC and papillary RCC tumor/stroma samples, run ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN for HDAC7, TEAD1 and MAML2 at the ACTA2/MYH11/TAGLN/CNN1 loci and at NOTCH1/HES1 target sites; if HDAC7 does not co-occupy MEF2 sites at these contractile genes in either tissue, or if TEAD1/MAML2 knockdown fails to shift the HMGXB4 contractile-gene signature in both VSMC and papillary RCC lines, the shared-module account fails.
caveats: 112 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance signal has limited independence; the blood-kidney tissue pairing means the module most plausibly acts in a shared vascular/stromal compartment rather than in tumor epithelium or cardiomyocytes directly; the tissue-generic exclusion list (STAT5B, E2F3, IRF8, ESR1, KLF6, IRF1, TFE3, STAT1, NCOA1, FOXO4, FOS, MEF2C) already removed the obvious blood/kidney master regulators, so this module is the tissue-specific residual, not leftover generic signal; the single-view exclusion list (TERF2, BACH1, CIC, IRX2, IRF8, HEY2, TCF15, ZNF77, STAT1, BMAL2, TFE3, MIXL1) confirms none of the carrying factors are single-cohort artifacts; KAT6A, GLI3, SOX10, SOX6, RARB, DLX3, MLXIPL and NCOA4 were left out of the programme because their target sets (hematopoietic/MOZ-complex, Hedgehog, neural-crest, chondrogenic, retinoic-acid, and lipogenic, respectively) do not fit this smooth-muscle/mechanotransduction module, even though some are individually concordant.
